title: AR Interior Design Preview Studio
description: The user operates an augmented-reality interior design workstation where a luxurious purple-gold damask chair sits in a virtual showroom. By placing oversized Khronos sunglasses onto a mannequin head, the user activates an AR lens mode that lets them cycle wall colors, reposition the chair, adjust spotlight intensity, and finally capture a snapshot of their curated room layout.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap with cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements an AR Interior Design Preview Studio. Scene setup: Build a simple rectangular showroom with a floor plane (light wood texture via MeshStandardMaterial), three visible walls (soft gray), and an open front. Load ChairDamaskPurplegold.glb and place it center-right on the floor. Load SunglassesKhronos.glb scaled up 3x and place them floating near a simple geometric mannequin head (a sphere on a cylinder) at the left side of the room. Add a warm SpotLight aimed at the chair and soft AmbientLight. Use OrbitControls with constrained vertical angle. Interactions (5 steps): Step 1 — The user clicks and drags the sunglasses onto the mannequin head (raycaster drag). When sunglasses snap within 0.5 units of the head, they attach and an AR overlay activates: a subtle green-tinted post-processing border appears using a screen-space CSS overlay with animated dashed border. Step 2 — With AR mode active, a floating UI panel appears with 4 color swatches. Clicking a swatch changes all three wall materials to that color with a smooth lerped transition over 0.5 seconds. Step 3 — The user can now click the chair to enter repositioning mode. In this mode, clicking any point on the floor plane moves the chair there with a smooth animation using THREE.Vector3.lerp over 30 frames. Step 4 — A slider control appears for the spotlight intensity (range 0.2 to 3.0). Dragging it updates the SpotLight.intensity in real time, casting visible shadow changes on the floor (enable shadow mapping with PCFSoftShadowMap on renderer, castShadow on the spotlight, receiveShadow on the floor). Step 5 — A capture button triggers a brief camera dolly-zoom animation (move camera forward while increasing FOV over 1 second then reversing), flash a white overlay, and display a toast message saying 'Design Snapshot Saved!'. Use HTML/CSS overlay elements for the UI panel, slider, and button. Ensure both GLB models are prominently visible and integral to the interaction flow.
